newsitem.title: USA: Britons in New York attend gala election events.
newsitem.headline: Britons in New York attend gala election events.

text.p: Britons in New York gathered in official and unofficial meetings on Thursday night, to watch election returns and update the only British government Internet site to record the results.

Among the 200,000 Britons in the New York metropolitan area, more than 1,000 were invited to British government offices in mid-town Manhattan, where large screens displayed results in several rooms and tallies were fed into the Internet in a room of computers. Royal marines opened the event with a "tattoo" of pipes and drums, and security was tight.

In contrast, facilities were sparse in a downtown basement club, called "Pravda" where several hundred trendy Labourites and their guests watched the results on small screens. They cheered loudly, smoked cigarettes, usually forbidden in public places in New York, and savored every moment of Tony Blair's apparent victory.

Harold Evans, head of Random House publishing and his wife, Tina Brown, editor of the New Yorker magazine, came. So did American actress-model Lauren Hutton as well as Bianca Jagger, the Nicaraguan ex-wife of Mick Jagger, among others.
